problem: The claim that bitonic sorting uses prefix sums inside its merge step is wrong. The bitonic merge is a fixed compare-exchange network; prefix sums are not part of it. A student who writes this in an exam loses marks.
fix: Delete the bitonic-sort clause. Write instead: 'The two-level scan is the version used for ranking, stream compaction, counting, radix sort, quicksort partitioning and load balancing.'

problem: 'the running total of all elements before it' describes an exclusive scan, but the formula in Section 2 (y_i = x₀ + … + x_i) is an inclusive scan that includes x_i itself. The two statements contradict each other.
fix: Say: 'Prefix sums, also called scan, give every element the running total of all elements up to and including it. (Some texts use the exclusive form, which leaves out the element itself and starts from x₀ = 0.)' State clearly that the chapter's y_i is the inclusive form.

where: Lead, 'Both ideas use the same doubling trick'
problem: For broadcast the number of processors holding the value doubles; for scan no processor count doubles — what doubles each step is the length of the input block each running total covers. Calling both 'the number of processors holding useful information doubles' is misleading.
fix: Say: 'Both use a doubling idea: in broadcast the number of holders doubles each step; in scan the length of the summed block doubles from d to 2d each step.'

problem: The answer writes 'T_p = O(1000 + 10) = O(1010)'. O(1010) is O(1) as notation, so the line is meaningless and a student may copy it as a result.
fix: Write: 'T_p ≈ n/p + log₂ p = 1000 + 10 = 1010 steps, i.e. T_p = O(n/p + log₂ p)'. Keep the big-O in symbols only.

problem: 'The total work is O(n)' counts only the block scans and the offset additions. The block totals are prefix summed by doubling, which costs about p⌈log₂ p⌉ additions, so strictly W = O(n + p log₂ p). The O(n) claim needs a condition on p.
fix: Add: 'W = O(n + p log₂ p), which is O(n) when p is at most about n/log₂ n; alternatively one processor scans the p block totals sequentially in O(p) time, giving W = Θ(n) for p ≤ n.'

problem: 'also called scan or all-sums' — 'all-sums' is not standard; the usual name is 'all-prefix-sums'.
